nvmlDeviceGetTotalEccErrors.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlDeviceGetTotalEccErrors(nvmlDevice_t device, nvmlMemoryErrorType_t errorType, nvmlEccCounterType_t counterType, unsigned long long * eccCounts)
nvmlDeviceGetTotalEccErrors.doc:
Retrieves the total ECC error counts for the device.

For Fermi or newer fully supported devices. Only applicable to devices with ECC. Requires *[`nvmlInforomObject_t::NVML_INFOROM_ECC`]* version 1.0 or higher. Requires ECC Mode to be enabled.

The total error count is the sum of errors across each of the separate memory systems, i.e. the total set of errors across the entire device.

See [nvmlMemoryErrorType_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gac5469bd68b9fdcf78734471d86becb24)

for a description of available error types.

See

[nvmlEccCounterType_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1ga08978d1c4fb52b6a4c72b39de144f1d9) for a description of available counter types.

See also

[nvmlDeviceClearEccErrorCounts()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceCommands.html#group__nvmldevicecommands_1ga92683374c66c6bb2fd4772262375a845).

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

errorType.doc: Flag that specifies the type of the errors.

counterType.doc: Flag that specifies the counter-type of the errors.

eccCounts.doc: Reference in which to return the specified ECC errors.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if *eccCounts* has been set
* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *device*, *errorType* or *counterType* is invalid, or *eccCounts* is NULL
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if the device does not support this feature

* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

nvmlDeviceGetUUID.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlDeviceGetUUID(nvmlDevice_t device, char * uuid, unsigned int length)
nvmlDeviceGetUUID.doc:
Retrieves the globally unique immutable UUID associated with this device, as a 5 part hexadecimal string, that augments the immutable, board serial identifier.

For all products.

The UUID is a globally unique identifier. It is the only available identifier for pre-Fermi-architecture products. It does NOT correspond to any identifier printed on the board. It will not exceed 96 characters in length (including the NULL terminator). See nvmlConstants::NVML_DEVICE_UUID_V2_BUFFER_SIZE.

When used with MIG device handles the API returns globally unique UUIDs which can be used to identify MIG devices across both GPU and MIG devices. UUIDs are immutable for the lifetime of a MIG device.

uuid.doc: Reference in which to return the GPU UUID.

length.doc: The maximum allowed length of the string returned in *uuid*.

nvmlDeviceSetAdaptiveTgpMode_v1.doc:
Request to enable or disable Adaptive TGP Mode for a GPU.

RUBIN_OR_NEWER% Requires root/admin privileges.

Adaptive TGP Mode assigns tailored power budgets to two binned GPU parts within the same module, reducing node-to-node and rack-to-rack performance variation. An out-of-band administrator policy may override the in-band request; use [nvmlDeviceGetAdaptiveTgpModeInfo_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceQueries.html#group__nvmldevicequeries_1gac47e7e50af086ef87af288395c960cfe) to query the arbitrated state.

See also

[nvmlDeviceGetAdaptiveTgpModeInfo_v1()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceQueries.html#group__nvmldevicequeries_1gac47e7e50af086ef87af288395c960cfe).

nvmlDeviceGetAddressingMode.doc:
Get the addressing mode for a given GPU.

Addressing modes can be one of:

1. HMM: System allocated memory (malloc, mmap) is addressable from the device (GPU), via software-based mirroring of the CPU’s page tables, on the GPU.
2. ATS: System allocated memory (malloc, mmap) is addressable from the device (GPU), via Address Translation Services. This means that there is (effectively) a single set of page tables, and the CPU and GPU both use them.
3. None: Neither HMM nor ATS is active.

For Turing or newer fully supported devices. Supported on Linux only.

mode.doc: Pointer to addressing mode of the device.

nvmlDeviceDiscoverGpus.doc:
Request the OS and the NVIDIA kernel driver to rediscover a portion of the PCI subsystem looking for GPUs that were previously removed.

The portion of the PCI tree can be narrowed by specifying a domain, bus, and device. If all are zeroes then the entire PCI tree will be searched. Please note that for long-running NVML processes the enumeration will change based on how many GPUs are discovered and where they are inserted in bus order.

In addition, all newly discovered GPUs will be initialized and their ECC scrubbed which may take several seconds per GPU. Also, all device handles are no longer guaranteed to be valid post discovery.

Must be run as administrator. For Linux only.

For Pascal or newer fully supported devices. Some Kepler devices supported.

nvmlDeviceRemoveGpu_v2.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlDeviceRemoveGpu_v2(nvmlPciInfo_t * pciInfo, nvmlDetachGpuState_t gpuState, nvmlPcieLinkState_t linkState)
nvmlDeviceRemoveGpu_v2.doc:
This method will remove the specified GPU from the view of both NVML and the NVIDIA kernel driver as long as no other processes are attached.

If other processes are attached, this call will return [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_IN_USE`] and the GPU will be returned to its original “draining” state. Note: the only situation where a process can still be attached after [nvmlDeviceModifyDrainState()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlZPI.html#group__nvmlzpi_1ga6e1b9572fb980fc4c24c4eb51ec440af) is called to initiate the draining state is if that process was using, and is still using, a GPU before the call was made. Also note, persistence mode counts as an attachment to the GPU thus it must be disabled prior to this call.

For long-running NVML processes please note that this will change the enumeration of current GPUs. For example, if there are four GPUs present and GPU1 is removed, the new enumeration will be 0-2. Also, device handles after the removed GPU will not be valid and must be re-established. Must be run as administrator. For Linux only.

For Pascal or newer fully supported devices. Some Kepler devices supported.

pciInfo.doc: The PCI address of the GPU to be removed.

gpuState.doc: Whether the GPU is to be removed, from the OS see [nvmlDetachGpuState_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDrainDefs.html#group__nvmldraindefs_1gad8049c64e43dc187b2e1bebf3ef79b64).

linkState.doc: Requested upstream PCIe link state, see [nvmlPcieLinkState_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDrainDefs.html#group__nvmldraindefs_1ga0590ae5cac2350595ed5de66266255f1).

* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *nvmlIndex* is invalid
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if the device doesn’t support this feature
* [NVML_ERROR_IN_USE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0acafd899d7203a855d056b38671404b54) if the device is still in use and cannot be removed

[`nvmlGpuOperationalEventLogLevel_t::NVML_GPU_OPERATIONAL_EVENT_LOG_LEVEL_ALL`] disables log-level filtering when used as a subscription threshold. nvmlDeviceRegisterEvents.doc:
Starts recording of events on a specified devices and add the events to specified [nvmlEventSet_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga608bba9ede7ea5526f43c04faab14c14).

For Fermi or newer fully supported devices. ECC events are available only on ECC-enabled devices (see [nvmlDeviceGetTotalEccErrors](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceQueries.html#group__nvmldevicequeries_1ga5ca6c7f177d7f3d89d05613a4cd30eb9)) Power capping events are available only on Power Management enabled devices (see [nvmlDeviceGetPowerManagementMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceQueries.html#group__nvmldevicequeries_1ga5576e74f8666b7e73ba851fceaea44a7))

For Linux only.

This call starts recording of events on specific device. All events that occurred before this call are not recorded. Checking if some event occurred can be done with [nvmlEventSetWait_v2](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gaa7bb0acbe65faf7beebd51120cf03d2e)

If function reports [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN`], event set is in undefined state and should be freed. If function reports [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`], event set can still be used. None of the requested eventTypes are registered in that case.

See also

[Event Types](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEventType.html#group__nvmleventtype)

See also

[nvmlDeviceGetSupportedEventTypes](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gac67e12f360199a40809522491d6cb0dd)

nvmlEventSetWait

nvmlEventSetGetContextCount_v1.doc:
Gets the number of context records for the most recent event returned by [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d) on this event set.

This count is tied to the event set, not to a caller-owned copy of [nvmlEventSetWait_v3_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlEventSetWait__v3__t.html#structnvmleventsetwait__v3__t). It is replaced by the next successful call to [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d) on the same event set.

For Turing or newer fully supported devices.

For Linux only.

See also

[nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d)

See also

[nvmlEventSetGetContextInfo_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gac891e3c87faeb65d84490bb300ab1d96)

[nvmlEventSetGetContextData_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga306730c7a72ade2755bcb92849f77230).

nvmlEventSetGetContextData_v1.doc:
Copies the raw payload for a context record from the most recent event returned by [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d).

Passing `params->data` as NULL performs a size query. In that case `params->dataSize` is set to the required payload size and the function returns [NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af7e0eae06744556cc832b7569489051f) when the payload is non-empty. If the context payload is empty, `params->dataSize` is set to 0 and the function returns [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3).

For Turing or newer fully supported devices.

For Linux only.

See also

[nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d)

See also

[nvmlEventSetGetContextCount_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gae061854f3d2d573dcaf4f8cfbd620b95)

See also

[nvmlEventSetGetContextInfo_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gac891e3c87faeb65d84490bb300ab1d96).

* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if arguments are invalid or `params->index` is out of range
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa1bfb13c6d0f00249b20f556c2d5d23f) if no event has been returned by [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d)
* [NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af7e0eae06744556cc832b7569489051f) if `params->data` is NULL or too small for a non-empty payload
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if this API is not available on the platform or driver

nvmlEventSetGetContextInfo_v1.doc:
Gets metadata for a context record from the most recent event returned by [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d).

The returned metadata identifies the NVML public interpretation, the source-defined context payload type, payload size, and payload format version. The raw payload for any context record can be copied with [nvmlEventSetGetContextData_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga306730c7a72ade2755bcb92849f77230). When `nvmlGpuOperationalEventContextType` names a type-specific accessor, callers may use that accessor instead. Metadata is replaced by the next successful call to [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d) on the same event set.

For Turing or newer fully supported devices.

For Linux only.

See also

[nvmlEventSetGetContextInfo_v1_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlEventSetGetContextInfo__v1__t.html#structnvmleventsetgetcontextinfo__v1__t)

See also

[nvmlEventSetGetContextCount_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gae061854f3d2d573dcaf4f8cfbd620b95)

See also

[nvmlEventSetGetContextData_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga306730c7a72ade2755bcb92849f77230).

params.doc: Context index and returned context metadata.

* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if arguments are invalid or `params->index` is out of range
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa1bfb13c6d0f00249b20f556c2d5d23f) if no event has been returned by [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d)
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if this API is not available on the platform or driver
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

nvmlEventSetGetGpuOperationalEventContex.doc:
Gets decoded GPU legacy-Xid context data for a context record from the most recent event returned by [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d).

This helper succeeds only for context records whose `nvmlGpuOperationalEventContextType` is [NVML_GPU_OPERATIONAL_EVENT_CONTEXT_TYPE_LEGACY_XID](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gga6ee6ca9ea1b75de85e5cf04f2eee56a6a12d96e54c05eae7cde2c923a44f15bb6). Other context records remain available through [nvmlEventSetGetContextData_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga306730c7a72ade2755bcb92849f77230).

For Turing or newer fully supported devices.

For Linux only.

See also

[nvmlEventSetGetGpuOperationalEventContextLegacyXid_v1_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlEventSetGetGpuOperationalEventContextLegacyXid__v1__t.html#structnvmleventsetgetgpuoperationaleventcontextlegacyxid__v1__t)

See also

[nvmlEventSetGetContextInfo_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gac891e3c87faeb65d84490bb300ab1d96)

See also

[nvmlEventSetGetContextData_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga306730c7a72ade2755bcb92849f77230).

params.doc: Context index and returned legacy-Xid data.

* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if arguments are invalid or `params->index` is out of range
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa1bfb13c6d0f00249b20f556c2d5d23f) if no event has been returned or the context is not a GPU legacy-Xid context
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if this API is not available on the platform or driver
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

nvmlEventSetRegisterGpuOperationalEvents.doc:
Adds a GPU Operational Event subscription to an event set.

This API is separate from [nvmlDeviceRegisterEvents](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga27b1fd1536a725f6792c15ebb0eb76ec). Calling this API opts the event set into the structured GPU Operational Event format for the target GPU UUID. Subscriptions are identified by *config*; registering the same subscription more than once is treated as success.

[nvmlDeviceRegisterEvents](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga27b1fd1536a725f6792c15ebb0eb76ec) and [nvmlEventSetRegisterGpuOperationalEvents_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga6cd4ca00b4b55d3e8952b17a3219626a) may both be used on the same event set. In that mixed-subscription model, NVML event-bit subscriptions continue to deliver event bits such as [nvmlEventTypeXidCriticalError](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEventType.html#group__nvmleventtype_1ga5c4ab639ab019151adc28eec22bbbba7), while GPU Operational Event subscriptions deliver [NVML_EVENT_DATA_TYPE_GPU_OPERATIONAL_EVENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gga97b62aece5507e283716b9f45e3dabe9a9e0085b77d4221f1fa675819446d71ba) records through [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d) with `eventType` set to [nvmlEventTypeNone](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEventType.html#group__nvmleventtype_1ga57c3938101e88a6cf0609a9595b37812). The same underlying incident may generate both an NVML event-bit notification and a structured notification.

This API supports GPU UUID subscriptions.

For Turing or newer fully supported devices.

For Linux only.

See also

[nvmlGpuOperationalEventConfig_v1_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlGpuOperationalEventConfig__v1__t.html#structnvmlgpuoperationaleventconfig__v1__t)

See also

[nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d)

See also

[nvmlEventSetFree](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga77fea3d629e72567121391453801185b).

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if the GPU Operational Event subscription was registered
* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized

nvmlEventSetWait_v2.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlEventSetWait_v2(nvmlEventSet_t set, nvmlEventData_t * data, unsigned int timeoutms)
nvmlEventSetWait_v2.doc:
Waits on events and delivers events.

For Fermi or newer fully supported devices.

If some events are ready to be delivered at the time of the call, function returns immediately. If there are no events ready to be delivered, function sleeps till event arrives but not longer than specified timeout. This function in certain conditions can return before specified timeout passes (e.g. when interrupt arrives)

On Windows, in case of Xid error, the function returns the most recent Xid error type seen by the system. If there are multiple Xid errors generated before nvmlEventSetWait is invoked then the last seen Xid error type is returned for all Xid error events.

On Linux, every Xid error event would return the associated event data and other information if applicable.

In MIG mode, if device handle is provided, the API reports all the events for the available instances, only if the caller has appropriate privileges. In absence of required privileges, only the events which affect all the instances (i.e. whole device) are reported.

This API does not currently support per-instance event reporting using MIG device handles.

See also

[Event Types](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEventType.html#group__nvmleventtype)

See also

[nvmlDeviceRegisterEvents](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga27b1fd1536a725f6792c15ebb0eb76ec).

nvmlEventSetWait_v3.doc:
Waits on an event set and returns the next event in the extended event format.

This API is the unified wait surface for NVML event-bit subscriptions registered with [nvmlDeviceRegisterEvents](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga27b1fd1536a725f6792c15ebb0eb76ec) and structured GPU Operational Event subscriptions registered with [nvmlEventSetRegisterGpuOperationalEvents_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga6cd4ca00b4b55d3e8952b17a3219626a).

The returned format is distinguished by `dataType` in *params*. If `dataType` is [NVML_EVENT_DATA_TYPE_NVML_EVENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gga97b62aece5507e283716b9f45e3dabe9aa1529ece25515945768d6ba6332a4213), the event came from the [nvmlDeviceRegisterEvents](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga27b1fd1536a725f6792c15ebb0eb76ec) path, `eventType` is an NVML event bit such as [nvmlEventTypeXidCriticalError](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEventType.html#group__nvmleventtype_1ga5c4ab639ab019151adc28eec22bbbba7), and the existing fields preserve their historical semantics. If `dataType` is [NVML_EVENT_DATA_TYPE_GPU_OPERATIONAL_EVENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gga97b62aece5507e283716b9f45e3dabe9a9e0085b77d4221f1fa675819446d71ba), the event came from the structured format, `eventType` is [nvmlEventTypeNone](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEventType.html#group__nvmleventtype_1ga57c3938101e88a6cf0609a9595b37812), and the structured metadata fields are populated.

When an event set contains only NVML event-bit subscriptions, this API normalizes those events into [nvmlEventSetWait_v3_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlEventSetWait__v3__t.html#structnvmleventsetwait__v3__t). When an event set contains both NVML event-bit and structured subscriptions, each successful call returns the next available event from either path. Clients should branch on `dataType` to determine which format was returned. An event set is not required to have structured GPU Operational Event subscriptions to be used with this API.

Context records for the returned event, if any, are made available through [nvmlEventSetGetContextCount_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gae061854f3d2d573dcaf4f8cfbd620b95), [nvmlEventSetGetContextInfo_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gac891e3c87faeb65d84490bb300ab1d96), and [nvmlEventSetGetContextData_v1](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga306730c7a72ade2755bcb92849f77230). Context records remain associated with the event set until the next successful call to [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d) on the same event set or until the event set is freed.

For Turing or newer fully supported devices.

For Linux only.

See also

[nvmlEventSetWait_v3_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlEventSetWait__v3__t.html#structnvmleventsetwait__v3__t)

nvmlSystemRegisterEvents.doc:
Starts recording of events on system and add the events to specified [nvmlSystemEventSet_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga2ed5fe735a1a0614f83373505699ac54).

For Linux only.

This call starts recording of events on specific device. All events that occurred before this call are not recorded. Checking if some event occurred can be done with [nvmlSystemEventSetWait](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga3e6b7ba3def8996fd9bdc643ca5d11e1)

If function reports [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN`], event set is in undefined state and should be freed. If function reports [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`], event set can still be used. None of the requested eventTypes are registered in that case.

NVML_FI_PWR_SMOOTHING_ADMIN_OVERRIDE_PRI.doc:
Current primary floor activation offset value in Watts for admin override.

If the target moving average falls below the secondary floor plus this offset, the primary floor will be activated.

Current primary floor activation window multiplier value for admin override.

This is the “X” ms time multiplier for the activation moving average window size. The activation moving average is compared against the (secondary floor + primary floor activation offset value) to determine if the controller should switch from the secondary floor to the primary floor. Setting this to 0 will disable switching to the secondary floor.

Current primary floor target window multiplier value for admin override.

This is the “X” ms time multiplier for the target moving average window size. When set to non-zero value, the target moving average power determines the primary floor. When set to 0, driver will use the Floor percentage instead to derive the primary floor.

NVML_FI_PWR_SMOOTHING_MIN_PRIMARY_FLOOR_.doc:
Minimum primary floor activation offset value in Watts.

This is the minimum primary floor activation offset accepted by the driver specified in Watts. This is a static field.

Minimum primary floor activation point value in Watts.

This is the minimum absolute raw value specified in Watts that the driver will use for switching between primary and secondary floor. This point is calculated as “secondary power floor +

primary floor activation offset”, and then computed value is floored to “min primary floor

activation point” by the driver at run time. This value is used to avoid setting of switch point too low accidentally.

NVML_FI_PWR_SMOOTHING_PRIMARY_POWER_FLOO.doc:
Current primary power floor value in Watts.

This value is calculated by doing “TMP ceiling value \* (% TMP floor value)”.

nvmlInitWithFlags.doc:
Initialize the NVML Library lazily, without allocating any device state, with additional init flags.

A variant of [nvmlInit_v2()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gace23f80e7fea03c289af95e8885af4c8), this will initialize the NVML Library state without enumerating any discovered devices. An option to pass in additional flags is provided to modify the behavior of NVML Library init. The usage of these flags can be obtained from NVML_INIT_FLAG_\*. These flags can be combined together.

Other than the “flags” parameter, this method is completely identical to [nvmlInit_v2()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gace23f80e7fea03c289af95e8885af4c8).

For all products.

See also

[nvmlShutdown()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gab019a8336c1459b53435941b89ab913f).

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if the NVML Library was properly initialized.
* [NVML_ERROR_DRIVER_NOT_LOADED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aef6f5ae0e66d50d4b9ce8b653307c443) if the NVIDIA driver is not running.
* [NVML_ERROR_NO_PERMISSION](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a4be33cb660536c94725ef79cae0c277c) if the NVML Library does not have permission to talk to the driver.
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) if there is an unexpected error.

nvmlInit_v2.doc:
Initialize the NVML Library lazily, without allocating any device state.

This will initialize the NVML Library state without enumerating any discovered devices. This will allow NVML to communicate with a device, even if other devices are in an unstable or bad state. Enumeration of a device can be done by obtaining the device handle via the nvmlDeviceGetHandleBy\* class of APIs.

This method needs to be called once before any usage of NVML Library APIs.

For all products.

See also

[nvmlShutdown()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gab019a8336c1459b53435941b89ab913f).

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if the NVML Library was properly initialized.
* [NVML_ERROR_DRIVER_NOT_LOADED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aef6f5ae0e66d50d4b9ce8b653307c443) if the NVIDIA driver is not running.
* [NVML_ERROR_NO_PERMISSION](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a4be33cb660536c94725ef79cae0c277c) if the NVML Library does not have permission to talk to the driver.
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) if there is an unexpected error.

nvmlShutdown.doc:
Shut down and cleanup NVML Library state.

This will shut down and cleanup NVML Library state by releasing all device and library resources previously allocated with [nvmlInit_v2()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gace23f80e7fea03c289af95e8885af4c8) or [nvmlInitWithFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gad39d57197d94dc6fdee9d01d13f486b5). This should be called after all NVML work is done, and once for each call to [nvmlInit_v2()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gace23f80e7fea03c289af95e8885af4c8) or [nvmlInitWithFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gad39d57197d94dc6fdee9d01d13f486b5).

Complete shutdown will only occur when the reference count of all prior NVML initializations reaches zero. No error will be reported if this is called more times than [nvmlInit_v2()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gace23f80e7fea03c289af95e8885af4c8) or [nvmlInitWithFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlInitializationAndCleanup.html#group__nvmlinitializationandcleanup_1gad39d57197d94dc6fdee9d01d13f486b5).

For all products.

fields.Returns:

* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the NVML Library was not previously initialized.
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) if there is an unexpected error.

nvmlDeviceGetGpuInstancePossiblePlacemen.doc:
Get GPU instance placements.

A placement represents the location of a GPU instance within a device. This API only returns all the possible placements for the given profile regardless of whether MIG is enabled or not. A created GPU instance occupies memory slices described by its placement. Creation of new GPU instance will fail if there is overlap with the already occupied memory slices.

For Ampere or newer fully supported devices. Supported on Linux only. Requires privileged user.

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

profileId.doc: The GPU instance profile ID. See [nvmlDeviceGetGpuInstanceProfileInfo](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlMultiInstanceGPU.html#group__nvmlmultiinstancegpu_1ga1611f0e6286feaaeea557126f460883f).

placements.doc: Returns placements allowed for the profile. Can be NULL to discover number of allowed placements for this profile. If non-NULL must be large enough to accommodate the placements supported by the profile.

count.doc: Returns number of allowed placemenets for the profile.

nvmlDeviceSetMigMode.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlDeviceSetMigMode(nvmlDevice_t device, unsigned int mode, nvmlReturn_t * activationStatus)
nvmlDeviceSetMigMode.doc:
Set MIG mode for the device.

For Ampere or newer fully supported devices. Requires root user.

This mode determines whether a GPU instance can be created.

This API may unbind or reset the device to activate the requested mode. Thus, the attributes associated with the device, such as minor number, might change. The caller of this API is expected to query such attributes again.

On certain platforms like pass-through virtualization, where reset functionality may not be exposed directly, VM reboot is required. *activationStatus* would return [NVML_ERROR_RESET_REQUIRED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a4a15657439f8a77195273139d70af0e4) for such cases.

*activationStatus* would return the appropriate error code upon unsuccessful activation. For example, if device unbind fails because the device isn’t idle, [NVML_ERROR_IN_USE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0acafd899d7203a855d056b38671404b54) would be returned. The caller of this API is expected to idle the device and retry setting the *mode*.

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

mode.doc: The mode to be set, [NVML_DEVICE_MIG_DISABLE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlMultiInstanceGPU.html#group__nvmlmultiinstancegpu_1gaef352db6814cf27f48026962a1535729) or [NVML_DEVICE_MIG_ENABLE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlMultiInstanceGPU.html#group__nvmlmultiinstancegpu_1ga87e02c42bbfdbf299ec05e380136a14d).

* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) If library has not been successfully initialized
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) If *device*,*mode* or *activationStatus* are invalid

* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) If *device* doesn’t support MIG mode

nvmlGpuInstanceGetComputeInstancePossibl.doc:
Get compute instance placements.

For Ampere or newer fully supported devices. Supported on Linux only. Requires privileged user.

A placement represents the location of a compute instance within a GPU instance. This API only returns all the possible placements for the given profile. A created compute instance occupies compute slices described by its placement. Creation of new compute instance will fail if there is overlap with the already occupied compute slices.

gpuInstance.doc: The identifier of the target GPU instance.

profileId.doc: The compute instance profile ID. See [nvmlGpuInstanceGetComputeInstanceProfileInfo](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlMultiInstanceGPU.html#group__nvmlmultiinstancegpu_1ga579a74d8b300147aa37ed4d926cd525a).

placements.doc: Returns placements allowed for the profile. Can be NULL to discover number of allowed placements for this profile. If non-NULL must be large enough to accommodate the placements supported by the profile.

count.doc: Returns number of allowed placemenets for the profile.

nvmlGpmMetricsGet.doc:
Calculate GPM metrics from two samples.

For Hopper or newer fully supported devices.

To retrieve metrics, the user must first allocate the two sample buffers at *metricsGet->sample1* and *metricsGet->sample2* by calling *[nvmlGpmSampleAlloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlGpmFunctions.html#group__nvmlgpmfunctions_1ga0b73578aaf211ce10eeedf2e6b863262)*. Next, the user should fill in the ID of each metric in *metricsGet->metrics*[i].metricId and specify the total number of metrics to retrieve in *metricsGet->numMetrics*, The version should be set to NVML_GPM_METRICS_GET_VERSION in *metricsGet->version*. The user then calls the *[nvmlGpmSampleGet()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlGpmFunctions.html#group__nvmlgpmfunctions_1ga3205260e0eca4b4711531d90033a08d5)* API twice to obtain 2 samples of counters.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) on success
* Nonzero NVML_ERROR_? enum on error

nvmlGpmMigSampleGet.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlGpmMigSampleGet(nvmlDevice_t device, unsigned int gpuInstanceId, nvmlGpmSample_t gpmSample)
nvmlGpmMigSampleGet.doc:
Read a sample of GPM metrics into the provided *gpmSample* buffer for a MIG GPU Instance.

After two samples are gathered, you can call nvmlGpmMetricGet on those samples to retrieve metrics

For Hopper or newer fully supported devices.

device.doc: Device to get samples for.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) on success
* Nonzero NVML_ERROR_? enum on error

nvmlGpmQueryDeviceSupport.doc:
Indicate whether the supplied device supports GPM.

For Hopper or newer fully supported devices.

device.doc: The device handle or MIG device handle to query for.

gpmSupport.doc: Structure to indicate GPM support *[nvmlGpmSupport_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlGpmSupport__t.html#structnvmlgpmsupport__t)*. Indicates GPM support per system for the supplied device.

fields.Returns:
* NVML_SUCCESS on success
* Nonzero NVML_ERROR_? enum if there is an error in processing the query

nvmlGpmQueryIfStreamingEnabled.doc:
Get GPM stream state.

For Hopper or newer fully supported devices. Supported on Linux, Windows TCC.

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if *current* GPM stream state were successfully queried
* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *device* is invalid or *state* is NULL
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if this query is not supported by the device

nvmlGpmSampleAlloc.doc:
Allocate a sample buffer to be used with NVML GPM .

You will need to allocate at least two of these buffers to use with the NVML GPM feature

For Hopper or newer fully supported devices.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) on success
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if an invalid pointer is provided
* [NVML_ERROR_MEMORY](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a0fc4fe3b647ffbd98240d57b9e11256c) if system memory is insufficient

The board limit (operating) policy is currently limiting the GPU clocks. Board limit policy is limiting clocks.

See also

bug 1997531 Display clock setting limited.

Clocks are as high as possible. No clock throttling.

Reliability.

The reliability policy is currently limiting the GPU clocks. Reliability policy is limiting clocks.

The clocks have been optimized to ensure not to exceed currently set power limits.

nvmlClocksEventReasonSwThermalSlowdown.doc:
SW Thermal Slowdown.

The current clocks have been optimized to ensure the following is true:

* Current GPU temperature does not exceed GPU Max Operating Temperature
* Current memory temperature does not exceeed Memory Max Operating Temperature Software thermal slowdown activated.

nvmlClocksEventReasonSyncBoost.doc:
Sync Boost.

This GPU has been added to a Sync boost group with nvidia-smi or DCGM in order to maximize performance per watt. All GPUs in the sync boost group will boost to the minimum possible clocks across the entire group. Look at the throttle reasons for other GPUs in the system to see why those GPUs are holding this one at lower clocks. Sync boost activated.

nvmlClocksThrottleReasonHwPowerBrakeSlow.doc:
HW Power Brake Slowdown (reducing the core clocks by a factor of 2 or more) is engaged.

This is an indicator of:

* External Power Brake Assertion being triggered (e.g. by the system power supply)

nvmlClocksThrottleReasonHwSlowdown.doc:
HW Slowdown (reducing the core clocks by a factor of 2 or more) is engaged.

This is an indicator of:

* temperature being too high
* External Power Brake Assertion is triggered (e.g. by the system power supply)
* Power draw is too high and Fast Trigger protection is reducing the clocks
* May be also reported during PState or clock change

nvmlDeviceWorkloadPowerProfileGetProfile.doc:
Get Performance Profiles Information.

For Blackwell or newer fully supported devices. See [nvmlWorkloadPowerProfileProfilesInfo_v1_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlWorkloadPowerProfileProfilesInfo__v1__t.html#structnvmlworkloadpowerprofileprofilesinfo__v1__t) for more information on the struct. The mask *perfProfilesMask* is bitmask of all supported mode indices where the mode is supported if the index is 1. Each supported mode will have a corresponding entry in the *perfProfile* array which will contain the *profileId*, the *priority* of this mode, where the lower the value, the higher the priority, and a *conflictingMask*, where each bit set in the mask corresponds to a different profile which cannot be used in conjunction with the given profile.

The API only sets the active preset profile based on the input profileId, and ignores the other parameters of the structure. Requires root/admin permissions.

For Blackwell or newer fully supported devices.

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

profile.doc: Reference to [nvmlPowerSmoothingProfile_v1_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlPowerSmoothingProfile__v1__t.html#structnvmlpowersmoothingprofile__v1__t). Note that only *profile->profileId* is used and the rest of the structure is ignored.

* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if device is invalid or structure was NULL

* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if this feature is not supported by the device

* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if this feature is not supported by the device

nvmlDevicePowerSmoothingUpdatePresetProf.doc:
Update the value of a specific profile parameter contained within [nvmlPowerSmoothingProfile_v1_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlPowerSmoothingProfile__v1__t.html#structnvmlpowersmoothingprofile__v1__t).

Requires root/admin permissions.

For Blackwell or newer fully supported devices.

nvmlSystemGetCPER_v1.doc:
Retrieves Common Platform Error Record (CPER) data.

Records are returned in a caller-supplied buffer. Iteration is driven by the *cursor* ([nvmlCPERCursor_v1_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlCPERCursor__v1__t.html#structnvmlcpercursor__v1__t)) struct: pass the same *cursor* on every call in a sequence; the implementation updates *cursor.handle*. Do not modify *cursor* between calls. To change *cursor.cperTypeMask* or *cursor.uuid*, set *cursor.handle* to [NVML_CPER_CURSOR_HANDLE_INIT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlCPER.html#group__nvmlcper_1gaa26e590f3970f4de3b45a8b1d9c9b88a) and call again (new iteration).

For a size query, call with *buffer* NULL and *bufferSize* 0; the function returns [NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af7e0eae06744556cc832b7569489051f) and sets *bufferSize* when records exist, or [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) with *bufferSize* set to 0 when there are no CPER records. Use *bufferSize* == 0 on return as the indicator for “no records” or “no more records”.

This API requires root privileges. Records are available from initialization.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) Buffer has been populated with CPER data, or *bufferSize* is 0 (no/more records).
* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) The library has not been successfully initialized.
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) *cper* is NULL, or *buffer* is NULL while *bufferSize* is non-zero.
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) The feature is not supported on this system.
* [NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af7e0eae06744556cc832b7569489051f) Buffer too small; *bufferSize* set to required size.
* [NVML_ERROR_NO_PERMISSION](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a4be33cb660536c94725ef79cae0c277c) Insufficient privileges.
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) An unexpected error occurred.

nvmlSystemGetCudaDriverVersion.doc:
Retrieves the version of the CUDA driver.

For all products.

The CUDA driver version returned will be retreived from the currently installed version of CUDA. If the cuda library is not found, this function will return a known supported version number.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if *cudaDriverVersion* has been set
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *cudaDriverVersion* is NULL

nvmlSystemGetCudaDriverVersion_v2.doc:
Retrieves the version of the CUDA driver from the shared library.

For all products.

The returned CUDA driver version by calling cuDriverGetVersion().

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if *cudaDriverVersion* has been set
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *cudaDriverVersion* is NULL
* [NVML_ERROR_LIBRARY_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a935c6648e17b975a15ed483bfc61956a) if *libcuda.so.1* or libcuda.dll is not found
* [NVML_ERROR_FUNCTION_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0acd798d96155e15f65a93701b1c2852d1) if *cuDriverGetVersion()* is not found in the shared library

nvmlSystemGetDriverBranch.doc:
Retrieves the driver branch of the NVIDIA driver installed on the system.

For all products.

The branch identifier is an alphanumeric string. It will not exceed 80 characters in length (including the NULL terminator). See nvmlConstants::NVML_SYSTEM_DRIVER_VERSION_BUFFER_SIZE.

branchInfo.doc: Pointer to the driver branch information structure *nvmlSystemDriverBranchInfo_t*.

length.doc: The maximum allowed length of the driver branch string.

* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *branchInfo* is NULL
* [NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af7e0eae06744556cc832b7569489051f) if *length* is too small
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

nvmlSystemGetTopologyGpuSet.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlSystemGetTopologyGpuSet(unsigned int cpuNumber, unsigned int * count, nvmlDevice_t * deviceArray)
nvmlSystemGetTopologyGpuSet.doc:
Retrieve the set of GPUs that have a CPU affinity with the given CPU number For all products.

Supported on Linux only.

count.doc: When zero, is set to the number of matching GPUs such that *deviceArray* can be malloc’d. When non-zero, *deviceArray* will be filled with *count* number of device handles.

deviceArray.doc: An array of device handles for GPUs found with affinity to *cpuNumber*.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if *deviceArray* or *count* (if initially zero) has been set

* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) an error has occurred in underlying topology discovery

nvmlUnitSetLedState.doc:
Set the LED state for the unit.

The LED can be either green (0) or amber (1).

For S-class products. Requires root/admin permissions.

This operation takes effect immediately.

**Current S-Class products don’t provide unique LEDs for each unit. As such, both front and back LEDs will be toggled in unison regardless of which unit is specified with this command.**

See [nvmlLedColor_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlUnitStructs.html#group__nvmlunitstructs_1ga03dd4a91d7b9dac971ce3304afcf9b71) for available colors.

See also

[nvmlUnitGetLedState()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlUnitQueries.html#group__nvmlunitqueries_1ga3320b0da8ac8ad02c463261c4c9c66d6).

unit.doc: The identifier of the target unit.

fields.Returns:

nvmlDeviceGetVgpuHeterogeneousMode.doc:
Get the vGPU heterogeneous mode for the device.

When in heterogeneous mode, a vGPU can concurrently host timesliced vGPUs with differing framebuffer sizes.

On successful return, the function returns *pHeterogeneousMode->mode* with the current vGPU heterogeneous mode. *pHeterogeneousMode->version* is the version number of the structure nvmlVgpuHeterogeneousMode_t, the caller should set the correct version number to retrieve the vGPU heterogeneous mode. *pHeterogeneousMode->mode* can either be [NVML_FEATURE_ENABLED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga11160f9605a87d03a59f987cccbd7b86a81902afbba2c53c2bcd3908b382cc96d) or [NVML_FEATURE_DISABLED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga11160f9605a87d03a59f987cccbd7b86afffb3df58081f0826b5337c2a128850e).

pHeterogeneousMode.doc: Pointer to the caller-provided structure of nvmlVgpuHeterogeneousMode_t.

nvmlDeviceGetVgpuTypeCreatablePlacements.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlDeviceGetVgpuTypeCreatablePlacements(nvmlDevice_t device, nvmlVgpuTypeId_t vgpuTypeId, nvmlVgpuPlacementList_t * pPlacementList)
nvmlDeviceGetVgpuTypeCreatablePlacements.doc:
Query the creatable vGPU placement ID of the vGPU type.

An array of creatable vGPU placement IDs for the vGPU type ID indicated by *vgpuTypeId* is returned in the caller-supplied buffer of *pPlacementList->placementIds*. Memory needed for the placementIds array should be allocated based on maximum instances of a vGPU type which can be queried via [nvmlVgpuTypeGetMaxInstances()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpu.html#group__nvmlvgpu_1gab4bc4b243fa1f77827ef63632f24d337). If the provided count by the caller is insufficient, the function will return [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`] along with the number of required entries in *pPlacementList->count*. The caller should then reallocate a buffer with the size of pPlacementList->count \* sizeof(pPlacementList->placementIds) and invoke the function again.

The creatable vGPU placement IDs may differ over time, as there may be restrictions on what type of vGPU the vGPU instance is running.

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

vgpuTypeId.doc: Handle to vGPU type. The vGPU type ID.

pPlacementList.doc: Pointer to the list of vGPU placement structure *nvmlVgpuPlacementList_t*.

nvmlDeviceGetVgpuTypeSupportedPlacements.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlDeviceGetVgpuTypeSupportedPlacements(nvmlDevice_t device, nvmlVgpuTypeId_t vgpuTypeId, nvmlVgpuPlacementList_t * pPlacementList)
nvmlDeviceGetVgpuTypeSupportedPlacements.doc:
Query the supported vGPU placement ID of the vGPU type.

The function returns an array of supported vGPU placement IDs for the specified vGPU type ID in the buffer provided by the caller at *pPlacementList->placementIds*. The required memory for the placementIds array must be allocated based on the maximum number of vGPU type instances, which is retrievable through [nvmlVgpuTypeGetMaxInstances()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpu.html#group__nvmlvgpu_1gab4bc4b243fa1f77827ef63632f24d337). If the provided count by the caller is insufficient, the function will return [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`] along with the number of required entries in *pPlacementList->count*. The caller should then reallocate a buffer with the size of pPlacementList->count \* sizeof(pPlacementList->placementIds) and invoke the function again.

To obtain a list of homogeneous placement IDs, the caller needs to set *pPlacementList->mode* to NVML_VGPU_PGPU_HOMOGENEOUS_MODE. For heterogeneous placement IDs, *pPlacementList->mode* should be set to NVML_VGPU_PGPU_HETEROGENEOUS_MODE. By default, a list of heterogeneous placement IDs is returned.

device.doc: Identifier of the target device.

vgpuTypeId.doc: Handle to vGPU type. The vGPU type ID.

pPlacementList.doc: Pointer to the vGPU placement structure *nvmlVgpuPlacementList_t*.

nvmlDeviceSetVgpuHeterogeneousMode.doc:
Enable or disable vGPU heterogeneous mode for the device.

When in heterogeneous mode, a vGPU can concurrently host timesliced vGPUs with differing framebuffer sizes.

API would return an appropriate error code upon unsuccessful activation. For example, the heterogeneous mode set will fail with error [NVML_ERROR_IN_USE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0acafd899d7203a855d056b38671404b54) if any vGPU instance is active on the device. The caller of this API is expected to shutdown the vGPU VMs and retry setting the *mode*. On KVM platform, setting heterogeneous mode is allowed, if no MDEV device is created on the device, else will fail with same error [NVML_ERROR_IN_USE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0acafd899d7203a855d056b38671404b54). On successful return, the function updates the vGPU heterogeneous mode with the user provided *pHeterogeneousMode->mode*. *pHeterogeneousMode->version* is the version number of the structure nvmlVgpuHeterogeneousMode_t, the caller should set the correct version number to set the vGPU heterogeneous mode.

nvmlDeviceGetActiveVgpus.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlDeviceGetActiveVgpus(nvmlDevice_t device, unsigned int * vgpuCount, nvmlVgpuInstance_t * vgpuInstances)
nvmlDeviceGetActiveVgpus.doc:
Retrieve the active vGPU instances on a device.

An array of active vGPU instances is returned in the caller-supplied buffer pointed at by *vgpuInstances*. The array element count is passed in *vgpuCount*, and *vgpuCount* is used to return the number of vGPU instances written to the buffer.

If the supplied buffer is not large enough to accommodate the vGPU instance array, the function returns [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`], with the element count of nvmlVgpuInstance_t array required in *vgpuCount*. To query the number of active vGPU instances, call this function with \*vgpuCount = 0. The code will return [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`], or [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_SUCCESS`] if no vGPU Types are supported.

For Kepler or newer fully supported devices.

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

vgpuCount.doc: Pointer which passes in the array size as well as get back the number of types.

vgpuInstances.doc: Pointer to array in which to return list of vGPU instances.

* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized

* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if vGPU is not supported by the device
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

nvmlDeviceGetCreatableVgpus.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlDeviceGetCreatableVgpus(nvmlDevice_t device, unsigned int * vgpuCount, nvmlVgpuTypeId_t * vgpuTypeIds)
nvmlDeviceGetCreatableVgpus.doc:
Retrieve the currently creatable vGPU types on a physical GPU (device).

An array of creatable vGPU types for the physical GPU indicated by *device* is returned in the caller-supplied buffer pointed at by *vgpuTypeIds*. The element count of nvmlVgpuTypeId_t array is passed in *vgpuCount*, and *vgpuCount* is used to return the number of vGPU types written to the buffer.

The creatable vGPU types for a device may differ over time, as there may be restrictions on what type of vGPU types can concurrently run on a device. For example, if only one vGPU type is allowed at a time on a device, then the creatable list will be restricted to whatever vGPU type is already running on the device.

If the supplied buffer is not large enough to accommodate the vGPU type array, the function returns [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`], with the element count of nvmlVgpuTypeId_t array required in *vgpuCount*. To query the number of vGPU types that can be created for the GPU, call this function with \*vgpuCount = 0. The code will return [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`], or [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_SUCCESS`] if no vGPU types are creatable.

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

vgpuCount.doc: Pointer to caller-supplied array size, and returns number of vGPU types.

vgpuTypeIds.doc: Pointer to caller-supplied array in which to return list of vGPU types.

* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *vgpuCount* is NULL
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if vGPU is not supported by the device
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

The array element count is passed in *pVgpuInstanceInfo->vgpuCount*, and *pVgpuInstanceInfo->vgpuCount* is used to return the number of vGPU instances written to the buffer.

If the supplied buffer is not large enough to accommodate the vGPU instance array, the function returns [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`], with the element count of nvmlVgpuInstance_t array required in *pVgpuInstanceInfo->vgpuCount*. To query the number of active vGPU instances, call this function with pVgpuInstanceInfo->vgpuCount = 0 and pVgpuInstanceInfo->vgpuTypeIds = NULL. The code will return [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`], or [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_SUCCESS`] if no vGPU Types are active.

nvmlGpuInstanceGetCreatableVgpus.doc:
Query the currently creatable vGPU types on a specific GPU Instance.

The function returns an array of vGPU types that can be created for a specified GPU instance. This array is stored in a caller-supplied buffer, with the buffer’s element count passed through *pVgpus->vgpuCount*. The number of vGPU types written to the buffer is indicated by *pVgpus->vgpuCount*. If the buffer is too small to hold the vGPU type array, the function returns [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`] and updates *pVgpus->vgpuCount* with the required element count.

To determine the creatable vGPUs for a GPU Instance, invoke this function with *pVgpus->vgpuCount* set to 0 and *pVgpus->vgpuTypeIds* as NULL. This will result in [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`] being returned, along with the count value in *pVgpus->vgpuCount*.

The creatable vGPU types may differ over time, as there may be restrictions on what type of vGPUs can concurrently run on the device.

nvmlGpuInstanceGetVgpuHeterogeneousMode.doc:
Get the vGPU heterogeneous mode for the GPU instance.

When in heterogeneous mode, a vGPU can concurrently host timesliced vGPUs with differing framebuffer sizes.

On successful return, the function returns *pHeterogeneousMode->mode* with the current vGPU heterogeneous mode. *pHeterogeneousMode->version* is the version number of the structure nvmlVgpuHeterogeneousMode_t, the caller should set the correct version number to retrieve the vGPU heterogeneous mode. *pHeterogeneousMode->mode* can either be [NVML_FEATURE_ENABLED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga11160f9605a87d03a59f987cccbd7b86a81902afbba2c53c2bcd3908b382cc96d) or [NVML_FEATURE_DISABLED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga11160f9605a87d03a59f987cccbd7b86afffb3df58081f0826b5337c2a128850e).

For Blackwell GB20x or newer fully supported devices.

nvmlGpuInstanceGetVgpuTypeCreatablePlace.doc:
Query the creatable vGPU placement ID of the vGPU type within a GPU instance.

For Blackwell GB20x or newer fully supported devices.

An array of creatable vGPU placement IDs for the vGPU type ID indicated by *pCreatablePlacementInfo->vgpuTypeId* is returned in the caller-supplied buffer of *pCreatablePlacementInfo->placementIds*. Memory needed for the placementIds array should be allocated based on maximum instances of a vGPU type per GPU instance which can be queried via [nvmlVgpuTypeGetMaxInstancesPerGpuInstance()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpu.html#group__nvmlvgpu_1gada4da6c2ec447f4f70c80089e1bf9ed9). If the provided count by the caller is insufficient, the function will return [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`] along with the number of required entries in *pCreatablePlacementInfo->count*. The caller should then reallocate a buffer with the size of pCreatablePlacementInfo->count \* sizeof(pCreatablePlacementInfo->placementIds) and invoke the function again. The creatable vGPU placement IDs may differ over time, as there may be restrictions on what type of vGPU the vGPU instance is running.

nvmlGpuInstanceSetVgpuHeterogeneousMode.doc:
Enable or disable vGPU heterogeneous mode for the GPU instance.

When in heterogeneous mode, a vGPU can concurrently host timesliced vGPUs with differing framebuffer sizes.

API would return an appropriate error code upon unsuccessful activation. For example, the heterogeneous mode set will fail with error [NVML_ERROR_IN_USE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0acafd899d7203a855d056b38671404b54) if any vGPU instance is active within the GPU instance. The caller of this API is expected to shutdown the vGPU VMs and retry setting the *mode*. On successful return, the function updates the vGPU heterogeneous mode with the user provided *pHeterogeneousMode->mode*. *pHeterogeneousMode->version* is the version number of the structure nvmlVgpuHeterogeneousMode_t, the caller should set the correct version number to set the vGPU heterogeneous mode.

nvmlVgpuInstanceGetEncoderSessions.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlVgpuInstanceGetEncoderSessions(nvmlVgpuInstance_t vgpuInstance, unsigned int * sessionCount, nvmlEncoderSessionInfo_t * sessionInfo)
nvmlVgpuInstanceGetEncoderSessions.doc:
Retrieves information about all active encoder sessions on a vGPU Instance.

An array of active encoder sessions is returned in the caller-supplied buffer pointed at by *sessionInfo*. The array element count is passed in *sessionCount*, and *sessionCount* is used to return the number of sessions written to the buffer.

If the supplied buffer is not large enough to accommodate the active session array, the function returns [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`], with the element count of [nvmlEncoderSessionInfo_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlEncoderSessionInfo__t.html#structnvmlencodersessioninfo__t) array required in *sessionCount*. To query the number of active encoder sessions, call this function with \*sessionCount = 0. The code will return [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_SUCCESS`] with number of active encoder sessions updated in \*sessionCount.

For Maxwell or newer fully supported devices.

vgpuInstance.doc: Identifier of the target vGPU instance.

sessionCount.doc: Reference to caller supplied array size, and returns the number of sessions.

sessionInfo.doc: Reference to caller supplied array in which the list of session information us returned.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if *sessionInfo* is fetched

* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *sessionCount* is NULL, or *vgpuInstance* is 0.

* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

nvmlVgpuInstanceGetVmDriverVersion.doc:
Retrieve the NVIDIA driver version installed in the VM associated with a vGPU.

The version is returned as an alphanumeric string in the caller-supplied buffer *version*. The length of the version string will not exceed 80 characters in length (including the NUL terminator). See nvmlConstants::NVML_SYSTEM_DRIVER_VERSION_BUFFER_SIZE.

[nvmlVgpuInstanceGetVmDriverVersion()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpu.html#group__nvmlvgpu_1ga70c07fd0417b39a4f342cdbc2d9b5ac0) may be called at any time for a vGPU instance. The guest VM driver version is returned as “Not Available” if no NVIDIA driver is installed in the VM, or the VM has not yet booted to the point where the NVIDIA driver is loaded and initialized.

For Kepler or newer fully supported devices.

version.doc: Caller-supplied buffer to return driver version string.

nvmlDeviceGetPgpuMetadataString.doc:
Returns the properties of the physical GPU indicated by the device in an ascii-encoded string format.

The caller passes in a buffer via *pgpuMetadata*, with the size of the buffer in *bufferSize*. If the string is too large to fit in the supplied buffer, the function returns [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`] with the size needed in *bufferSize*.

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

pgpuMetadata.doc: Pointer to caller-supplied buffer into which *pgpuMetadata* is written.

* [NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af7e0eae06744556cc832b7569489051f) *pgpuMetadata* buffer is too small, required size is returned in *bufferSize*
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) If *bufferSize* is NULL or *device* is invalid; if *pgpuMetadata* is NULL and the value of *bufferSize* is not 0.
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) If vGPU is not supported by the system
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) On any unexpected error

nvmlDeviceGetVgpuMetadata.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlDeviceGetVgpuMetadata(nvmlDevice_t device, nvmlVgpuPgpuMetadata_t * pgpuMetadata, unsigned int * bufferSize)
nvmlDeviceGetVgpuMetadata.doc:
Returns a vGPU metadata structure for the physical GPU indicated by *device*.

The structure contains information about the GPU and the currently installed NVIDIA host driver version that’s controlling it, together with an opaque data section containing internal state.

The caller passes in a buffer via *pgpuMetadata*, with the size of the buffer in *bufferSize*. If the *pgpuMetadata* structure is too large to fit in the supplied buffer, the function returns [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`] with the size needed in *bufferSize*.

device.doc: The identifier of the target device.

pgpuMetadata.doc: Pointer to caller-supplied buffer into which *pgpuMetadata* is written.

* [NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af7e0eae06744556cc832b7569489051f) pgpuMetadata buffer is too small, required size is returned in *bufferSize*
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *bufferSize* is NULL or *device* is invalid; if *pgpuMetadata* is NULL and the value of *bufferSize* is not 0.
