* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

nvmlDeviceGetVgpuSchedulerCapabilities.doc:
Returns the vGPU scheduler capabilities.

The list of supported vGPU schedulers returned in *[nvmlVgpuSchedulerCapabilities_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlVgpuSchedulerCapabilities__t.html#structnvmlvgpuschedulercapabilities__t)* is from the NVML_VGPU_SCHEDULER_POLICY_\*. This list enumerates the supported scheduler policies if the engine is Graphics type. The other values in *[nvmlVgpuSchedulerCapabilities_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlVgpuSchedulerCapabilities__t.html#structnvmlvgpuschedulercapabilities__t)* are also applicable if the engine is Graphics type. For other engine types, it is BEST EFFORT policy. If ARR is supported and enabled, scheduling frequency and averaging factor are applicable else timeSlice is applicable.

For Pascal or newer fully supported devices.

* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) If *pCapabilities* is NULL or *device* is invalid

nvmlGetVgpuCompatibility.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlGetVgpuCompatibility(nvmlVgpuMetadata_t * vgpuMetadata, nvmlVgpuPgpuMetadata_t * pgpuMetadata, nvmlVgpuPgpuCompatibility_t * compatibilityInfo)
nvmlGetVgpuCompatibility.doc:
Takes a vGPU instance metadata structure read from [nvmlVgpuInstanceGetMetadata()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpuMigration.html#group__nvmlvgpumigration_1ga3cc63b652f40453a06c95b3a81ea4004), and a vGPU metadata structure for a physical GPU read from [nvmlDeviceGetVgpuMetadata()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpuMigration.html#group__nvmlvgpumigration_1ga15523975b561b05888c707054238e140), and returns compatibility information of the vGPU instance and the physical GPU.

The caller passes in a buffer via *compatibilityInfo*, into which a compatibility information structure is written. The structure defines the states in which the vGPU / VM may be booted on the physical GPU. If the vGPU / VM compatibility with the physical GPU is limited, a limit code indicates the factor limiting compatability. (see [nvmlVgpuPgpuCompatibilityLimitCode_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpuMigration.html#group__nvmlvgpumigration_1gaec041a4dadb43447ef886d7f4f9e5abc) for details).

Note: vGPU compatibility does not take into account dynamic capacity conditions that may limit a system’s ability to boot a given vGPU or associated VM.

vgpuMetadata.doc: Pointer to caller-supplied vGPU metadata structure.

pgpuMetadata.doc: Pointer to caller-supplied GPU metadata structure.

compatibilityInfo.doc: Pointer to caller-supplied buffer to hold compatibility info.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) vGPU metadata structure was successfully returned
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) If *vgpuMetadata* or *pgpuMetadata* or *bufferSize* are NULL
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) On any unexpected error

nvmlGetVgpuVersion.doc:
Query the ranges of supported vGPU versions.

This function gets the linear range of supported vGPU versions that is preset for the NVIDIA vGPU Manager and the range set by an administrator. If the preset range has not been overridden by [nvmlSetVgpuVersion](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpuMigration.html#group__nvmlvgpumigration_1gaec13e4f85b5ca3f90d28b5538c314bb5), both ranges are the same.

The caller passes pointers to the following [nvmlVgpuVersion_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlVgpuVersion__t.html#structnvmlvgpuversion__t) structures, into which the NVIDIA vGPU Manager writes the ranges:

1. *supported* structure that represents the preset range of vGPU versions supported by the NVIDIA vGPU Manager.
2. *current* structure that represents the range of supported vGPU versions set by an administrator. By default, this range is the same as the preset range.

supported.doc: Pointer to the structure in which the preset range of vGPU versions supported by the NVIDIA vGPU Manager is written.

current.doc: Pointer to the structure in which the range of supported vGPU versions set by an administrator is written.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) The vGPU version range structures were successfully obtained.
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) The API is not supported.
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) The *supported* parameter or the *current* parameter is NULL.
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) An error occurred while the data was being fetched.

nvmlSetVgpuVersion.doc:
Override the preset range of vGPU versions supported by the NVIDIA vGPU Manager with a range set by an administrator.

This function configures the NVIDIA vGPU Manager with a range of supported vGPU versions set by an administrator. This range must be a subset of the preset range that the NVIDIA vGPU Manager supports. The custom range set by an administrator takes precedence over the preset range and is advertised to the guest VM for negotiating the vGPU version. See [nvmlGetVgpuVersion](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpuMigration.html#group__nvmlvgpumigration_1ga67a2f3379d2078e23e1c6e0dc48efe0c) for details of how to query the preset range of versions supported.

This function takes a pointer to vGPU version range structure [nvmlVgpuVersion_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlVgpuVersion__t.html#structnvmlvgpuversion__t) as input to override the preset vGPU version range that the NVIDIA vGPU Manager supports.

After host system reboot or driver reload, the range of supported versions reverts to the range that is preset for the NVIDIA vGPU Manager.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) The preset range of supported vGPU versions was successfully overridden.
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) The API is not supported.
* [NVML_ERROR_IN_USE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0acafd899d7203a855d056b38671404b54) The range was not overridden because a VM is running on the host.
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) The *vgpuVersion* parameter specifies a range that is outside the range supported by the NVIDIA vGPU Manager or if *vgpuVersion* is NULL.

nvmlVgpuInstanceGetMetadata.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlVgpuInstanceGetMetadata(nvmlVgpuInstance_t vgpuInstance, nvmlVgpuMetadata_t * vgpuMetadata, unsigned int * bufferSize)
nvmlVgpuInstanceGetMetadata.doc:
Returns vGPU metadata structure for a running vGPU.

The structure contains information about the vGPU and its associated VM such as the currently installed NVIDIA guest driver version, together with host driver version and an opaque data section containing internal state.

[nvmlVgpuInstanceGetMetadata()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVgpuMigration.html#group__nvmlvgpumigration_1ga3cc63b652f40453a06c95b3a81ea4004) may be called at any time for a vGPU instance. Some fields in the returned structure are dependent on information obtained from the guest VM, which may not yet have reached a state where that information is available. The current state of these dependent fields is reflected in the info structure’s [nvmlVgpuGuestInfoState_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlVirtualGpuEnums.html#group__nvmlvirtualgpuenums_1ga695f1fec53a6439ccf2ef5adb207c054) field.

The VMM may choose to read and save the vGPU’s VM info as persistent metadata associated with the VM, and provide it to Virtual GPU Manager when creating a vGPU for subsequent instances of the VM.

The caller passes in a buffer via *vgpuMetadata*, with the size of the buffer in *bufferSize*. If the vGPU Metadata structure is too large to fit in the supplied buffer, the function returns [`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE`] with the size needed in *bufferSize*.

vgpuInstance.doc: vGPU instance handle.

vgpuMetadata.doc: Pointer to caller-supplied buffer into which vGPU metadata is written.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) vGPU metadata structure was successfully returned
* [NVML_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SIZE](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af7e0eae06744556cc832b7569489051f) vgpuMetadata buffer is too small, required size is returned in *bufferSize*
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *bufferSize* is NULL or *vgpuInstance* is 0; if *vgpuMetadata* is NULL and the value of *bufferSize* is not 0.
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa1bfb13c6d0f00249b20f556c2d5d23f) if *vgpuInstance* does not match a valid active vGPU instance on the system
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

nvmlDeviceGetVgpuInstancesUtilizationInf.doc:
Retrieves recent utilization for vGPU instances running on a physical GPU (device).

For Kepler or newer fully supported devices.

Reads recent utilization of GPU SM (3D/Compute), framebuffer, video encoder, video decoder, jpeg decoder, and OFA for vGPU instances running on a device. Utilization values are returned as an array of utilization sample structures in the caller-supplied buffer pointed at by *vgpuUtilInfo->vgpuUtilArray*. One utilization sample structure is returned per vGPU instance, and includes the CPU timestamp at which the samples were recorded. Individual utilization values are returned as “unsigned int” values in [nvmlValue_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/unionnvmlValue__t.html#unionnvmlvalue__t) unions. For Maxwell or newer fully supported devices.

Reads recent utilization of GPU SM (3D/Compute), framebuffer, video encoder, and video decoder for processes running on vGPU instances active on a device. Utilization values are returned as an array of utilization sample structures in the caller-supplied buffer pointed at by *utilizationSamples*. One utilization sample structure is returned per process running on vGPU instances, that had some non-zero utilization during the last sample period. It includes the CPU timestamp at which the samples were recorded. Individual utilization values are returned as “unsigned int” values.

To read utilization values, first determine the size of buffer required to hold the samples by invoking the function with *utilizationSamples* set to NULL. Set it to 0 to read utilization based on all the samples maintained by the driver’s internal sample buffer. Set lastSeenTimeStamp to a timeStamp retrieved from a previous query to read utilization since the previous query.

nvmlVgpuInstanceGetAccountingStats.signature: nvmlReturn_t nvmlVgpuInstanceGetAccountingStats(nvmlVgpuInstance_t vgpuInstance, unsigned int pid, nvmlAccountingStats_t * stats)
nvmlVgpuInstanceGetAccountingStats.doc:
Queries process’s accounting stats.

For Maxwell or newer fully supported devices.

Accounting stats capture GPU utilization and other statistics across the lifetime of a process, and can be queried during life time of the process or after its termination. The time field in [nvmlAccountingStats_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlAccountingStats__t.html#structnvmlaccountingstats__t) is reported as 0 during the lifetime of the process and updated to actual running time after its termination. Accounting stats are kept in a circular buffer, newly created processes overwrite information about old processes.

See [nvmlAccountingStats_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlAccountingStats__t.html#structnvmlaccountingstats__t) for description of each returned metric. List of processes that can be queried can be retrieved from [nvmlVgpuInstanceGetAccountingPids](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlUtil.html#group__nvmlutil_1ga56b4ba4899287099b940744622be76a5).

vgpuInstance.doc: The identifier of the target vGPU instance.

pid.doc: Process Id of the target process to query stats for.

stats.doc: Reference in which to return the process’s accounting stats.

fields.Returns:
* [NVML_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa24d587db29324840a89a40c00c727f3) if stats have been successfully retrieved
* [NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae054644f6612bf2ffb3f0e68379ec612) if the library has not been successfully initialized
* [NVML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a9658b0b4a4ced32a9148abb63d234aff) if *vgpuInstance* is 0, or *stats* is NULL
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0aa1bfb13c6d0f00249b20f556c2d5d23f) if *vgpuInstance* does not match a valid active vGPU instance on the system or *stats* is not found
* [NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0af9e8a97d37f2e4efdf330ef938663e81) if the vGPU doesn’t support this feature or accounting mode is disabled
* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

* [NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceEnums.html#group__nvmldeviceenums_1gga06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0ae08ac94f623461b8f5156bbb2c1eeb2a) on any unexpected error

nvmlCPERCursor_v1_t.doc:
CPER query and cursor parameters.

Groups the filter options and opaque read position used to iterate through CPER records.

Cursor semantics for iterative calls:

* Pass the same *[nvmlCPERCursor_v1_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlCPERCursor__v1__t.html#structnvmlcpercursor__v1__t)* (i.e. the same *cursor*) on every call in a single iteration sequence.
* Do not modify this struct between calls.
* To change *cperTypeMask* or *uuid*, set *handle* to [NVML_CPER_CURSOR_HANDLE_INIT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlCPER.html#group__nvmlcper_1gaa26e590f3970f4de3b45a8b1d9c9b88a) and call again with the updated filter (this starts a new iteration).

cperTypeMask.doc: [IN] Types of records to access. Bitmask of [nvmlCPERType_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlCPER.html#group__nvmlcper_1ga296184470c92b02f2f7b977002cab29d) values. To change, reset *handle* to [NVML_CPER_CURSOR_HANDLE_INIT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlCPER.html#group__nvmlcper_1gaa26e590f3970f4de3b45a8b1d9c9b88a).

uuid.doc: [IN] UUID of target to filter records for. Required for [NVML_CPER_ACCESS_TYPE_GPU](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlCPER.html#group__nvmlcper_1gga296184470c92b02f2f7b977002cab29dab7609250ce8df51411ed32aa84cae0f6). To change, reset *handle* to [NVML_CPER_CURSOR_HANDLE_INIT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlCPER.html#group__nvmlcper_1gaa26e590f3970f4de3b45a8b1d9c9b88a).

handle.doc: [IN/OUT] Opaque handle tracking read position. Initialize to [NVML_CPER_CURSOR_HANDLE_INIT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlCPER.html#group__nvmlcper_1gaa26e590f3970f4de3b45a8b1d9c9b88a) on first call; pass the same *[nvmlCPERCursor_v1_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/structnvmlCPERCursor__v1__t.html#structnvmlcpercursor__v1__t)* on the next call to continue. Caller must not interpret or modify.

nvmlEventSetWait_v3_t.doc:
Parameters for waiting on an event set with [nvmlEventSetWait_v3](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga1b5cb5f8475ae63ec93ed0cdb9240c8d).

This structure supplies the wait timeout and returns either NVML event-bit or structured event data. For NVML event-bit data, `dataType` is [NVML_EVENT_DATA_TYPE_NVML_EVENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gga97b62aece5507e283716b9f45e3dabe9aa1529ece25515945768d6ba6332a4213), `eventType` contains the NVML event bit, fields such as `eventData`, `gpuInstanceId`, and `computeInstanceId` preserve existing semantics, and structured-only fields are set to 0 or empty values. For structured GPU Operational Events, `dataType` is [NVML_EVENT_DATA_TYPE_GPU_OPERATIONAL_EVENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1gga97b62aece5507e283716b9f45e3dabe9a9e0085b77d4221f1fa675819446d71ba), `eventType` is set to [nvmlEventTypeNone](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEventType.html#group__nvmleventtype_1ga57c3938101e88a6cf0609a9595b37812), and the structured metadata fields are populated.

Clients that subscribe to both NVML event-bit and structured formats on the same event set should branch on `dataType` to determine which format was returned. During the transition period, the same underlying incident may generate both an NVML event-bit notification and a structured notification.

timeoutMs.doc: [in] Maximum amount of time to wait, in milliseconds.

dataType.doc: [out] [nvmlEventDataType_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEvents.html#group__nvmlevents_1ga97b62aece5507e283716b9f45e3dabe9) value indicating which event-data format is populated.

eventData.doc: [out] Xid code for [nvmlEventTypeXidCriticalError](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlEventType.html#group__nvmleventtype_1ga5c4ab639ab019151adc28eec22bbbba7), or 0 when not applicable.

May contain newer severity values not named in this header. [`nvmlOperationalEventSeverity_t::NVML_OPERATIONAL_EVENT_SEVERITY_ALL`] for NVML event-bit events.

nvmlGetMemoryLimits_v1_t.doc:
Describes the current memory limits that are set for the device.

This structure holds the necessary information that can be used to get the current soft and hard memory limits of a device.

The softLimit is the amount of memory that is guaranteed before allocations may fail due to memory pressure.

The hardLimit is the maximum amount of memory that can be allocated.

This should be cross-referenced with [nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo_v2](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceQueries.html#group__nvmldevicequeries_1ga030c167e7242fb3af1c5051a6c4a2d44) while in that cgroup to see how much memory is actually available to allocate for the device.

No limit is set when softLimit is 0 and hardLimit is [NVML_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_MAX](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceStructs.html#group__nvmldevicestructs_1ga5362488408778945a74cc245519f3dd7).

nameSpace.doc: [in] Full path to sysfs cgroup file name.

softLimit.doc: [out] Currently set soft memory limit in Bytes.

hardLimit.doc: [out] Currently set hard memory limit in Bytes.

metricId.doc: IN: NVML_GPM_METRIC_? define of which metric to retrieve.

nvmlReturn.doc: OUT: Status of this metric. If this is nonzero, then value is not valid.

value.doc: OUT: Value of this metric. Is only valid if nvmlReturn is 0 ([`nvmlReturn_t::NVML_SUCCESS`]).

metricInfo.doc: OUT: Metric name and unit. Those can be NULL if not defined.

numMetrics.doc: IN: How many metrics to retrieve in metrics[].

metrics.doc: IN/OUT: Array of metrics. Set metricId on call. See nvmlReturn and value on return.

bIsPresent.doc: Set if this utilization domain is present on this GPU.

percentage.doc: Percentage of time where the domain is considered busy in the last 1-second interval.

incThreshold.doc: Utilization threshold that can trigger a perf-increasing P-State change when crossed.

decThreshold.doc: Utilization threshold that can trigger a perf-decreasing P-State change when crossed.

The power supply state is a human readable string that equals “Normal” or contains a combination of “Abnormal” plus one or more of the following:

Describes the memory limits that can be set for the device.

This structure holds the necessary information that can be used to set the soft and hard memory limits of a device.

The softLimit is the amount of memory that is guaranteed before allocations may fail due to memory pressure.

The hardLimit is the maximum amount of memory that can be allocated.

This should be cross-referenced with [nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo_v2](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceQueries.html#group__nvmldevicequeries_1ga030c167e7242fb3af1c5051a6c4a2d44) while in that cgroup to see how much memory is actually available to allocate for the device.

To clear the limits, set softLimit to 0, and hardLimit to [NVML_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT_MAX](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlDeviceStructs.html#group__nvmldevicestructs_1ga5362488408778945a74cc245519f3dd7). Removing the cgroup will also clear any limits.
